spike_swarm_sim.objects.world_object module¶

class spike_swarm_sim.objects.world_object.WorldObject(model_file, position, orientation, static=True, controller=None, tangible=True, luminous=False, trainable=False, z_offset=None)[source]¶

Bases: abc.ABC

Base class for abstract world objects or entities. This class is the most basic class of world entities and only implements abstract properties of objects. It does not implement positions, orientations, and so on. This class must not be directly instantiated and all world objects have to inherit from it indirectly.

Parameters

  • model_file (str) – name of the file where the model of the entity is stored.

  • position –

  • orientation –

  • static (bool) – whether the object is static or can move.

  • controller (Controller) – controller, if any, defining object behavior. If the object cannot be controlled, then controller=None.

  • tangible (bool) – whether the object has collisions or not.

  • luminous (bool) – whether the object emits light or not.

  • trainable (bool) – whether the object controller can be trained (not really used yet).

  • z_offset (float) – z-axis offset of the entity position. It is only valid for 3D entities. If entity is not 3D, then it should be left as None.

Variables

  • physics_client (Engine) – physics and render client used in the simulations.

  • id (int) – unique identifier of the entity (should not be changed unless strictly needed).

step(neighborhood, reward=None, perturbations=None)[source]¶

Step method of the robots. It is composed by the following main steps:

  1. Firstly steps and reads all the sensors in order to perceive the environment.

  2. The robot executes its controller in order to compute the actions based on the sensory information.

  3. The actions are stored as planned actions to be eventually executed.

Parameters

  • neighborhood (list) – list filled with the neighboring world objects.

  • reward (float) – reward to be fed to the controller update rules, if any.

  • perturbations (list) – list of PostProcessingPerturbation to apply to the stimuli before controller step. If there are no perturbations to apply the paramter is None.

Returns

state and action tuple of the current timestep. Both of them are expressed as a dict with the sensor/actuator name and the corresponding stimuli/action.

plan_actions(actions)[source]¶
actuate(neighborhood)[source]¶

Executes the previously planned actions in order to be processed in the world.

Parameters

Computes the observed stimuli by steping each of the active sensors one by one.

spike_swarm_sim.objects.light_source module¶

class spike_swarm_sim.objects.light_source.LightSource(position, orientation, *args, color='red', range=1.0, z_offset=0.0, **kwargs)[source]¶

Bases: spike_swarm_sim.objects.world_object.WorldObject

Class of the light source entity. It is an intangible entity that isotropically emits light of a certain color and up to a defined range. Even though they are represented as 3D or 2D balls, it is just displayed in that way for visualization purposes. They are actually point lights without mass. The emitted light can be sensed by robots through their light_sensors.

Parameters

  • color (str) – color of the light.

  • range (float) – coverage range of the light.

  • z_offset (int) – offset of the z-axis position of the point light.

step(neighborhood)[source]¶

Step method of the light sou ce. Even though lights are not technically controlled, they can

have a ‘virtual controller’ for allowing custom behaviours such as mobile lights or preys in the predator and prey game. The controller can be implemented just as in the robots.

param list neighborhood

list filled with the neighboring entities.

class spike_swarm_sim.objects.wall.Wall(*args, height=1, width=5, **kwargs)[source]¶

Bases: spike_swarm_sim.objects.world_object.WorldObject

Class of wall objects, with parametrizable height and width. The mass is large enough so that robots cannot move them. Its main use is to constrain the environment arena, but they can be also instantiated as regular walls in arbitrary positions.

Parameters

  • position –

  • height (float) – height in metres of the wall.

  • width (float) – width in metres of the wall.
